title: 360 Secure Browser
summary: 360 Secure Browser is a cross-platform freeware web browser developed by Qihoo 360. It primarily uses the Blink engine for rendering, with an optional Trident engine for compatibility mode. The browser supports Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS. It is notable for its dual-engine architecture, default Chrome-like rendering, and the ability to spoof user-agent strings to mimic Chrome or Internet Explorer. The browser's market presence in China was historically significant, though usage statistics are contested. It has been involved in controversies regarding hidden mechanisms and aggressive promotion tactics.

mechanisms.title: Dual-engine rendering
mechanisms.explanation: The browser defaults to the Blink engine for webpage rendering, which is the same engine used by Google Chrome. When running in compatibility mode, it switches to the Trident engine found in Internet Explorer to render legacy webpages.

mechanisms.title: User-agent spoofing
mechanisms.explanation: To aid compatibility and masking, the browser spoofs its user-agent string, presenting itself as either Google Chrome or Internet Explorer. This makes it difficult for developers to target or identify the browser using standard sniffing techniques.
